title: Canonical Borel–Serre isomorphisms of rational intersection line distributions for constant-rank bundles over locally projective flat families
author: Dennis Eriksson; Gerard Freixas i Montplet
difficulty_reason: The classical Borel--Serre equality in the Chow ring does not specify a canonical isomorphism of relative line distributions or its compatibility with trivializations. Beyond the cited splitting principles and Deligne pairings, the authors construct coherent Chern-category and intersection-distribution operations, including Whitney, rank and restriction isomorphisms and control of the rational sign ambiguity. The selected proof then descends a rank-inductive isomorphism through flags and compares the newly constructed restriction trivialization with the independent Koszul acyclicity trivialization using the full exterior-filtration and commutative-diagram chain.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem9.5 in the Section9 setting: X to S locally projective, faithfully flat of finite presentation with pure relative dimension n, and E a vector bundle of constant rank r. There is a canonical rational intersection line-distribution isomorphism [ch(lambda_-1(E))]=[c_r(E dual) td(E dual)^-1], compatible with short exact sequences/admissible filtrations and identifying both canonical trivializations for a regular nowhere-vanishing section of E dual. Full new rank-induction and Koszul/trivialization comparison109–112 read. Published splitting principles reference15 Theorem2.10/Remark2.12 and general-base Deligne pairings references8 appendix/11 are explicitly traced in62–67; formal background Picardification32–33 and named MacLane/Thomason coherence retained. Routine diagram consequences whose maps are explicitly constructed are recorded as such, not assistant proof repairs. No integral sign-free assertion or general Deligne–Riemann–Roch isomorphism is claimed. Corollary9.6 closed-immersion application is not separately counted.
